claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, and lived approximately from c. 310–320 to 403.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis in Palestine and spent his early years as a monk in Egypt before returning to found a monastery near his birthplace.
Epiphanius was elected bishop of Salamis (Constantia), the metropolis of Cyprus, in 367 and held the post until his death.
Epiphanius served as bishop for nearly forty years and travelled widely to combat heresies.
The Index discipulorum is attributed to Epiphanius in manuscript tradition, with the title 'Τοῦ ἁγίου Ἐπιφανίου ἀρχιεπισκόπου Κύπρου' (Of the holy Epiphanius, archbishop of Cyprus).
The work is also known as 'Index discipulorum' or 'Περὶ τῶν οʹ ἀποστόλων' (On the Seventy Apostles).
The Index discipulorum lists the twelve apostles and seventy disciples, providing names, relationships, and episcopal sees where applicable.
The Clavis Patrum Graecorum assigns the Index discipulorum the number CPG 3780.2.
The Index discipulorum was transmitted alongside related works including an 'Index apostolorum' and appendices that expand the list of disciples.

The work provides valuable information for understanding early Christian traditions about the apostles and seventy disciples, including their supposed missionary destinations and episcopal appointments.
